_readme.purpose: Ground truth for the 10 candidate-authored cases in evaluation/custom_cases/.
_readme.design_intent: These cases were written to exercise behaviours the supplied 12 do not reach: a per-day ICU cap, several caps binding at once, PARTIALLY_ADMISSIBLE, continuity credit that is granted but still insufficient, two clauses pulling in opposite directions, and robustness to irrelevant attributes.
_readme.how_expected_outcomes_were_established: Identical method to expected_public.json: the governing clause was located in the supplied wording and applied by hand before the engine was run. 'clause_basis' records the provision and page so the label can be checked independently.

clause_basis: Sub limits (p.7): room capped at 1% of INR 400,000 = INR 4,000/day x 3 days (72 hours) = INR 12,000 against INR 11,000 claimed, so the cap does not bind.
Cover 2 and Cover 3 (p.7): fees INR 40,000 against a INR 100,000 cap; medicines INR 55,000 against a INR 160,000 cap.
58 months of continuous coverage clear every waiting period; cholecystitis is on no exclusion list.

required_evidence.must_contain: Normal Room expenses: 1.0% of Basic Sum Insured
We will pay Reasonable and Customary charges

CUS-002.scenario: Several category sub-limits bind at once, including the per-day ICU cap
clause_basis: Sub limits (p.7): ICU capped at 2% of Basic Sum Insured per day = INR 6,000/day x 7 days (168 hours) = INR 42,000 against INR 90,000 claimed; INR 48,000 deducted.
Cover 2 (p.7): fees capped at 25% of INR 300,000 = INR 75,000 against INR 95,000 claimed; INR 20,000 deducted.
Cover 3 (p.7): consumables capped at 40% of INR 300,000 = INR 120,000 against INR 140,000 claimed; INR 20,000 deducted.
Cover 4 (p.8): ambulance capped at the lesser of 1% of Sum Insured (INR 3,000) and INR 1,000 = INR 1,000 against INR 2,500 claimed; INR 1,500 deducted.
Total deduction INR 89,500. Pre/post expenses at 10 and 25 days fall inside the 30/60-day windows.

required_evidence.must_contain: Intensive Care/ Therapeutic Unit expenses: 2% of Basic Sum Insured
subject to a limit of 25% of Sum Assured
subject to a limit of 40% Sum Insured
Ambulance charges in connection with any admissible claim limited to

clause_basis: Exclusion 7 (p.9): 'Dental treatment or surgery of any kind' is excluded without qualification.
The 30-hour admission is a valid hospitalisation, so the claim fails on the treatment category alone, not on the admission.

required_evidence.must_contain: Dental treatment or surgery of any kind

clause_basis: Exclusion 3 (p.9): hernia is expressly listed among the conditions excluded in the first year of the cover.
Only 6 months of coverage have elapsed and there is no prior insurer continuity, so the NB waiver on p.9 is unavailable.

required_evidence.must_contain: first year of operation of the insurance cover

clause_basis: Definitions, Hospital (p.3): the facility is not a network provider and neither registration nor minimum-criteria compliance is evidenced.
Definitions, Medically Necessary (p.4): medical necessity is explicitly unestablished.
Exclusion 1 (p.8): pre-existing status is null, so the 48-month waiting period cannot be evaluated.
Three independent conditions precedent are unresolved and only a claim form was supplied.

required_evidence.must_contain: Hospital means any institution established for in-patient care

CUS-006.scenario: Part of the claim falls outside a policy time window
clause_basis: Scope of Cover, Note (p.8): pre-hospitalisation is reimbursed for a maximum of 30 days before admission and post-hospitalisation for a maximum of 60 days after discharge.
The case records 45 days and 90 days, so INR 12,000 of pre-hospitalisation and INR 18,000 of post-hospitalisation expenses fall outside the windows and are not payable.
The hospitalisation itself is fully covered and no category cap binds, so the claim is partially rather than wholly admissible.

required_evidence.must_contain: Pre-Hospitalisation up to a maximum of 30 days

CUS-006.notes: The excluded portion is reported as a non-payable component rather than as a capped amount, which is what distinguishes PARTIALLY_ADMISSIBLE from ADMISSIBLE_WITH_LIMITS.

CUS-007.scenario: Continuity credit granted but still insufficient
clause_basis: Exclusion 1 (p.8): the pre-existing disease waiting period is reduced by the number of continuous preceding years of coverage under the previous health insurance policy.
Three prior years are credited (database and claim history received, previous sum insured equal at INR 500,000), giving 6 + 36 = 42 effective months.
42 months is still short of the 48 months the policy requires, so the claim is not payable.

required_evidence.must_contain: Pre-existing diseases will not be covered until 48 months
reduced by the number of Your continuous preceding years

CUS-007.notes: Guards against two opposite errors: ignoring continuity credit entirely, and granting the waiver merely because prior cover exists.

CUS-008.scenario: Two clauses pull in opposite directions
clause_basis: NB4 (p.7): dialysis is expressly named among the treatments covered where the stay is under 24 hours, so the 5-hour admission qualifies.
Exclusion 3 (p.9): dialysis for renal failure carries a first-year waiting period, but 46 months of coverage have elapsed, so it does not bite.
No cap binds: fees INR 6,000 against a 25% cap of INR 87,500; consumables INR 14,000 against a 40% cap of INR 140,000.

required_evidence.must_contain: first year of operation of the insurance cover

CUS-008.notes: A short admission that looks like an out-patient visit but is expressly covered; the engine must reconcile a covering clause and an excluding clause rather than stopping at the first one it retrieves.

CUS-009.scenario: Domiciliary treatment with no qualifying circumstance evidenced
clause_basis: Definitions, Domiciliary Treatment (p.2): cover requires either that the patient cannot be moved to a hospital or that no hospital room was available.
Both fields are null, so neither limb is established and the condition precedent fails.
The treatment itself is not excluded, so rejection would be wrong; abstention is the correct behaviour.

CUS-010.scenario: Irrelevant attributes must not influence the decision
clause_basis: Sub limits (p.7): room capped at 1% of INR 800,000 = INR 8,000/day x 4 days (96 hours) = INR 32,000 against INR 40,000 claimed; INR 8,000 deducted.
No other cap binds: fees INR 70,000 against INR 200,000; consumables INR 120,000 against INR 320,000.

The case carries loyalty tier, star rating, parking availability, ward wifi, preferred language, marketing opt-in, referral source and internal notes. None appears in the policy and none may affect the outcome.

required_evidence.must_contain: Normal Room expenses: 1.0% of Basic Sum Insured

CUS-010.notes: Directly tests RULE 9. The expected deduction is identical to what the same claim would produce with the irrelevant attributes stripped out.
